name: IEC read-only memory (ROM)
summary: IEC element marked ROM with grouped address inputs and data outputs that read the addressed word.
description: A ROM is drawn with the ROM qualifier, usually followed by its organisation such as 256x8. Address inputs are grouped with a binary grouping bracket marked A, and data outputs carry an A label to show they deliver the addressed word. Enable inputs often control three-state outputs.

On control drawings ROM symbols document lookup tables, character generators or firmware storage on logic boards. The organisation figure tells a reviewer the address range and data width at a glance.
The symbol does not show the stored content. The content reference, such as a firmware or table file revision, should be noted next to the symbol.
readingNotes: Organisation such as 256x8 gives words by width.
Data outputs carry the A label.
drawingChecklist: Group address inputs with A notation.
distinction: RAM adds write inputs; ROM outputs only.
